newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Policeman shot, two raped in Australian siege.
newsitem.headline: Policeman shot, two raped in Australian siege.

text.p: Australian police said on Wednesday they had charged a man with sexually assaulting a teenaged boy after a bizarre eight-hour siege during which a policeman was shot in the neck and a woman was raped.
The 27-year-old man was also charged with breaching parole and was remanded to appear in court on Friday on the sexual assault charge, a Queensland state police spokesman said.

The man, who had taken 14 hostages at different stages of the siege, was overpowered by police early on Wednesday in Mackay, a tropical city 800 km (500 miles) northwest of Brisbane on the Queensland coast.
"Bizarre is a word that really fits this case," the spokesman told Reuters.
Up to 40 shots from a .357 mm calibre pistol were fired by the gunman during the siege, one of which struck a policeman from a tactical response group.
The policeman was flown to nearby Townsille Hospital and was in a satisfactory condition after undergoing surgery on a neck wound, the spokesman said.

Police said the siege began when a man abducted a 16-year-old boy on Tuesday, took him to a hotel and sexually assaulted him. They said he then took the boy at gunpoint to a suburban shopping centre where he bought ammunition and a large hunting knife.
The boy escaped and the gunman then stopped a man and a woman in a car and told them to drive him to a nearby apartment block, where police said he took another four people hostage.

Two men and a woman managed to escape during the night but another woman was raped. The gunman took the woman he had raped to another apartment block across the street where she was released after he took another seven people hostage.
The gunman was overpowered by police early on Wednesday as he tried to steal a car.
Letty Karambasis, a resident in the second apartment block, told reporters several shots were fired when the man attempted to steal a car while holding a young woman hostage.
"You never knew if a bullet was going to come through your window or not," Karambasis said. "He (the gunman) was so cunning, I didn't see him at all."
